title: Add pick-conditioned placement head

hypothesis.statement: The placement prediction lacks explicit dependence on the selected pick point and local post-pick visual state

intervention.description: Condition the placement head on selected pick coordinates and local visual features while preserving the pick/place action API
intervention.estimated_cost: One short profile run plus one fixed-seed training run

validation_steps.expected_result: Valid pick/place outputs and no simulator assertion

validation_steps.description: Evaluate frozen held-out split by placement perturbation bin

context_fixed: Fixed simulator version and physics configuration
Same pick/place action API and training budget
context_varied: Policy architecture: baseline vs pick-conditioned placement head

predictions.expected_pattern: No material decline relative to baseline
Little change: intervention targets placement, not pick

disconfirming_patterns.description: Improvement appears only in-distribution and disappears on the held-out split
disconfirming_patterns.implication: Apparent gain may be overfitting, not pick-place coupling
disconfirming_patterns.suggested_model_expansion: Leakage/regularization diagnostic before any architecture change

disconfirming_patterns.description: Baseline and conditioned policies fail similarly given an oracle pick point
disconfirming_patterns.implication: Missing pick-conditioning is unlikely to be the main mechanism
disconfirming_patterns.suggested_model_expansion: Test visual-state ambiguity with an oracle state or segmentation intervention

adopt_if: Held-out placement robustness improves by at least 5 percentage points
Action feasibility remains within 1 percentage point of baseline
reject_if: No measurable improvement under matched initial states
Gains disappear under the frozen evaluation protocol
Oracle-pick comparison indicates visual ambiguity dominates

rollback_description: Disable conditioned head via config and retain baseline checkpoint
